stem_book: N₂(g) and H₂(g), taken in 1:3 mole ratio, are allowed to react in a thermally insulated closed vessel at given temperature and pressure for the formation of NH₃(g) [N₂(g) + 3H₂(g) ⇌ 2NH₃(g) + 22.4 kcal]. If He(g) is added at equilibrium at constant pressure, then which is/are correct? (a) Concentration of N₂(g), H₂(g) and NH₃(g) decrease (b) Moles of NH₃(g) decreases (c) The extent of cooling depends on amount of He(g) added (d) Concentration of N₂ and H₂ increases and concentration of NH₃ decreases
key: (a), (b), (c) all three concentrations fall; moles of NH₃ fall; the cooling depends on the amount of He
reason: Coordinator: 1:3 feed and insulated vessel added to make the key hold - not used. Added 1:3 feed ratio and insulated vessel: (a) fails for a large H₂ excess with high conversion (numerically, pN₂ then rises on dilution); (c) needs the cooling to be observable. Judgement call - drop if such assumptions are not acceptable
work: He at const P dilutes; Δng = −2 -> backward (endothermic, cools, more He -> more shift); 1:3 feed: pNH₃ = c·pN₂², 4pN₂ + pNH₃ falls -> all partial pressures fall
